event.canonical_title: COP31 Climate Talks Commence in Antalya Amid Global Challenges
event.summary: The United Nations COP31 climate summit has officially opened in Antalya, Turkey. This year's discussions come in the wake of severe heatwaves and floods experienced globally, alongside new challenges posed by the ongoing war in Iran, which is affecting energy supplies worldwide.

timeline.title: COP31 Climate Talks Collapse Over Fossil Fuel Dispute
timeline.summary: The COP31 climate talks in Turkey ended in failure after a heated disagreement regarding fossil fuels. The European Union and other nations rejected a draft agreement that omitted any references to fossil fuels, which have become a contentious issue during the negotiations. This breakdown raises concerns about the future of the climate deal.
key_facts: COP31 climate talks took place in Turkey.
The talks broke down on November 22, 2026.
The EU rejected a draft agreement that excluded fossil fuels.

event_overview.title: About Climate Change
event_overview.subject: Climate Change
event_overview.summary: COP31 was the 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference, the annual negotiating session for parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). It brought governments together in Antalya, Türkiye, alongside accredited observers and other stakeholders, to negotiate and advance international action on emissions reductions, adaptation and climate finance under the UN climate treaties.

facts.label: Dates and venue
facts.value: The conference was scheduled for 9-20 November 2026 at the Antalya EXPO Center in Soğucaksu, Antalya, Türkiye.

facts.label: Institutional basis
facts.value: COP31 was the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the 1992 UNFCCC, the framework treaty that underpins the international climate-negotiation process and is the parent treaty to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

facts.label: Meeting format
facts.value: The gathering also convened CMP21, the meeting of parties to the Kyoto Protocol, and CMA8, the meeting of parties to the Paris Agreement; these linked bodies consider matters under their respective treaties.

facts.label: Hosts and leadership
facts.value: Türkiye hosted the conference, with Murat Kurum nominated as COP31 President; Australia’s Chris Bowen served as President of Negotiations under the Türkiye-Australia partnership arrangements.

facts.label: Participants and access
facts.value: Parties to the UNFCCC sent leaders and negotiators, while accredited observer groups—including UN bodies, intergovernmental organizations, NGOs, business representatives, scientists, Indigenous Peoples and youth—could participate under UNFCCC procedures. Official negotiating meetings were held in the registered-participant Blue Zone; the host-managed Green Zone was intended for public-facing activities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows the conference’s opening and its reported collapse over fossil-fuel language; it does not attempt to catalogue every negotiation text, side event, national statement or issue discussed during COP31.

related_events.summary: During the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, Greenpeace International unveiled a giant Trojan Horse overflowing with plastic waste. The installation, created by Danish artist Thomas Dambo, serves as a striking protest highlighting the environmental impact of plastics.
